key_insight: PISA is a preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM optimizer that delivers provable convergence for deep nonconvex models under minimal assumptions while supporting heterogeneous data and flexible preconditioners, and it empirically outperforms standard optimizers.
problem_solved: Training deep models reliably and efficiently when data is heterogeneous and when one wants to use varied preconditioners—settings where existing optimizers lack both practical robustness and theoretical convergence guarantees.
method: Preconditioned stochastic ADMM framework: splits optimization into modular subproblems and applies per-block preconditioners to handle heterogeneity across data/parameters.
Inexact subproblem solves with controlled error: permits cheaper, approximate updates (e.g., truncated inner solvers) while maintaining global convergence.
Theoretical convergence under minimal assumptions: rigorous analysis for nonconvex objectives that guides practical choices of preconditioners and step rules.
impact: Provides practitioners a robust, general-purpose optimizer that reduces tuning and instability when training across heterogeneous datasets or architectures, offering theoretical guarantees plus better empirical performance compared with common baselines.
visual_elements: Algorithm flow diagram: ADMM split with stochastic updates and preconditioner blocks annotated (showing per-block updates and information flow).
Performance chart: loss/accuracy vs. epochs comparing PISA to Adam/SGD/ADAMW across several tasks (highlight faster/stabler convergence).
Heterogeneous-data schematic: multiple data sources/devices feeding into a shared model with per-block preconditioning icons.
Icon set: badges for 'Provable Convergence', 'Low Inner Solve Cost (Inexact)', and 'Flexible Preconditioning' to summarize strengths.
paper_title: Preconditioned inexact stochastic ADMM for deep models
paper_authors: Shenglong Zhou, Ouya Wang, Ziyan Luo, Yongxu Zhu, Geoffrey Ye Li
